facts.statement: Grabauornis was an extinct genus of enantiornithean birds that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Grabauornis is an extinct genus of enantiornitheans from the Early Cretaceous of China.

facts.statement: The species Grabauornis lingyuanensis was named and described in 2014 by Johan Dalsätt, Per Ericson, and Zhou Zhonghe.
facts.quote: The type species, Grabauornis lingyuanensis, was named and described in 2014 by Johan Dalsätt, Per Ericson and Zhou Zhonghe.

facts.statement: The specific name lingyuanensis refers to the city of Lingyuan in the Liaoning province of China where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the place where it was found; the city of Lingyuan in the Lianoning province of China.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in the Yixian Formation, which dates to the Aptian age of 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossil, holotype IVPP V14595, was found in a layer of the Yixian Formation which dates to the Aptian, at an age of 125 million years.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a well-preserved skeleton that is compressed onto a single plate.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a well-preserved skeleton, compressed onto a single plate.

facts.statement: Grabauornis has a unique sternum where the center extends further back than the fan-shaped side wings.
facts.quote: Grabauornis shows a unique combination of differentiating traits. The center of the back of the sternum plate extends further back than the side wings, the latter are fan-shaped.

facts.statement: Grabauornis had a relatively short head equipped with small, conical teeth.
facts.quote: It also has a relatively short head with small, conical teeth.

facts.statement: Grabauornis had robust second and third finger phalanges, a third metacarpal extending beyond the second, and a hand shorter than the ulna.
facts.quote: As for the arms and hands; the second and third phalanges of the second finger are quite robust, the third metacarpal extends further than the second and the hand is shorter than the ulna.

facts.statement: The shoulder blade of Grabauornis was long, narrow, and tapered towards the top.
facts.quote: Besides that, the shoulder blade is long and narrow and tapers towards the top.

facts.statement: Grabauornis had a humerus length of 95% of its ulna, which is an average ratio compared to other enantiornitheans.
facts.quote: Grabauornis has a humerus that is 95% of the length of the ulna. In most enantiornitheans the values are between 77 and 125%, so Grabauornis has an average ratio.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Grabauornis had a good ability to fly because its humerus-to-ulna ratio was below the 130% threshold required for ground-dwelling.
facts.quote: According to the descriptors, this indicates a good ability to fly; only above 130% the animal would have to remain on the ground.

facts.statement: Grabauornis possessed an alula, a thumb feather that likely served as a nose vane, confirming its flying ability.
facts.quote: This ability would be confirmed by the possession of an alula, a thumb feather that could serve as a nose vane.

facts.statement: Grabauornis lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Grabauornis belongs to the parent group Euenantiornithes.
